clue.text: Take a retrograde step and cheat when selling car?

definitions.meaning: to go back to an older, worse state of affairs
a dishonest dealer winds back the mileage reading to make a used car look less driven

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reverting to the past, and literally describes winding back an odometer, which a crooked dealer does.

clue.text: Way Father is elevated to highest position open to him?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the words way and father turns them to read upward

parts.note: a way of doing something is a mode
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A priestly father rises to the highest office he could aspire to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is elevated' turns MODE + POP upward, giving POPEDOM; the definition only works for a Catholic priest, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the top rank available to a Catholic priest, the 'Father' of the surface.

clue.text: Finely tune television, initially faint

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of television

parts.note: a faint signal or sound is weak

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts a television whose picture is faint.
explanation.definitionFit: To make small precise adjustments is to fine-tune something.

clue.text: Element — the second I kept in here (not in US)

definitions.text: Element — the second I kept in here (not in US)

parts.words: Element — the second I kept in here (not in US)
parts.note: a metal whose British spelling keeps a second letter I that the American spelling drops

explanation.walkthrough: Americans write the metal as aluminum, without the second I; British spelling keeps it.
explanation.definitionFit: The light metallic element is spelt differently in Britain and the United States, differing by one letter I.

clue.text: Something not experienced by Miss Beale — or Buss?

definitions.text: Something not experienced by Miss Beale
definitions.meaning: an old rhyme about two Victorian headmistresses, Miss Buss and Miss Beale, says Cupid's darts they do not feel
buss is an old word for a smacking embrace of the lips

explanation.walkthrough: Frances Buss and Dorothea Beale were famous British pioneers of girls' schooling, mocked in a rhyme for their spinsterhood; 'Buss' here is the common noun, not the lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Buss is an archaic synonym for a peck on the lips, which the rhyme implies the spinster headmistresses never had.

clue.text: Male carried by roan he's broken, perhaps

definitions.text: Male carried by roan he's broken, perhaps

indicators.note: the letter for male is borne inside the rearranged letters, as a rider is carried
the words roan he's are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man rides a roan horse that he has broken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ROANHES into HORSEAN, and 'carried by' puts M inside it; the whole clue also describes a rider on a roan he trained.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a man carried by a horse such as a roan he has trained.

clue.text: Criminal caught going over castle

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going over another sits above it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the castle in chess is also called a rook

explanation.surface: A criminal is caught breaking into a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a dishonest person, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Thinks nothing, initially, about writer in public transport

indicators.note: initially puts the letter for nothing at the very start

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing

indicators.note: about means the verb's letters go round the writing tool

parts.note: muses means thinks or ponders
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about nothing in particular while riding a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'initially' are the two indicators; 'Thinks' looks like the main verb of the surface but is just a synonym, and 'writer' is the pen point, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Large passenger road vehicles were once called by this fuller name before it was shortened to bus.

clue.text: Entertaining result of performing bars of music

definitions.text: Entertaining result of performing bars of music

parts.words: Entertaining result of performing bars of music
parts.note: amateurs singing to backing tracks in bars, the drinking kind, entertain or embarrass the crowd

explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like musical measures but means pubs where amateurs sing along to recorded accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing popular songs over recorded backing, often in pubs, is a form of light entertainment.

clue.text: Previous incumbent comes back in place of rector, initially

indicators.note: in places the verb for returning inside the other letters

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for place
O is a clipped form of of, as in o'clock

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of rector

parts.note: something that recurs comes back again

explanation.surface: A former vicar returns to stand in for the rector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RECURS inside P, O, R; O for 'of' is the dialect clipping seen in o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A predecessor is the person who held a post before the present holder.

clue.text: One entitled to have new order accepted by soldiers

indicators.note: the rearranged word is taken in by the soldiers' letters

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: putting the letters of new in a fresh order rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone has a right to see a new order accepted by the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is the anagram signal and 'accepted by' the container; 'new order' reads like a political phrase, and OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person with the legal right to possess something.

clue.text: Child repeatedly turned back animal

indicators.note: turned back reverses the doubled word for a child
repeatedly says the word for child appears twice

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A child keeps turning back to look at an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives KIDKID and 'turned back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small African antelope.

clue.text: Slyly look at a work that's incomplete, easy to see through

parts.note: to peek is to take a sly look

indicators.note: the word for a work is missing its last letter

parts.note: a book is a written work

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a look at an unfinished book that is easy to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's incomplete' cuts the final K from BOOK. 'easy to see through' sounds like a book easy to understand but means a revealing garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A peekaboo garment is semi-transparent or has holes that reveal the skin.

clue.text: Spy chief is to attack unsuitable worker

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
a fit is a sudden attack, of coughing or rage

explanation.surface: An intelligence boss is about to go for an employee who is not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-suited to their job or surroundings does not belong there.

clue.text: Such a show-off crams late, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that crams late is only one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A know-all is someone who crams the night before an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CRAMSLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all who flaunts cleverness is this informal type of person.

clue.text: Scottish author given a hearing in town across border

indicators.note: given a hearing means the author's name is to be listened to, not read

parts.note: Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish historian and essayist

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer gets an audience in a town just over the border.
explanation.walkthrough: CARLISLE is an English city in Cumbria, just south of the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cumbrian city lies just across the border from Scotland.

clue.text: Dudley's a place in the Midlands

definitions.meaning: Dudley is, by title: Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite, was made an earl
a city in the English East Midlands

explanation.walkthrough: Dudley is itself a Midlands town, which steers you to read the clue as one geographical statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley was created Earl of the county of that name, and its county town is an East Midlands city.

clue.text: Formal procedures giving support-to officer

parts.note: pro means in favour of, a supporter
Col is short for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: Official rules govern how support is given to an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Official etiquette or rules of conduct are a code of proper practice.

clue.text: Weapon, possibly mine

definitions.meaning: a directional anti-personnel explosive device of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is the explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Highland broadsword and to a modern anti-personnel mine.

clue.text: Cowered, surrounded by a large number of Romans

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ringed means encircled

explanation.surface: Someone shrank back when hemmed in by a horde of Roman soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a large number of Romans' is a Roman numeral, not a crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or shrink back in fear is to cower.

clue.text: American beauty queen becoming wife?

parts.note: beauty pageant winners are titled Miss followed by a place
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A pageant winner goes on to become someone's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: A Miss US title-holder would be a beauty queen; the question mark warns that the definition is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is a colloquial term for one's spouse.

clue.text: Support ready for immediate use

definitions.meaning: to ... a friend is to back them
kept in reserve, as a spare ready to go

explanation.definitionFit: To stand by someone is to support them, and a reserve item is kept on standby for use.

clue.text: Eventually getting a ton on board -it's very close

indicators.note: on board means taken inside the phrase for eventually

parts.note: in time means eventually

explanation.surface: A ship finally takes on a ton of cargo in a tight finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts A and T inside IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Close friends or a close relationship can be called intimate.

clue.text: Precocious girl married the first man to appear

parts.note: in Genesis, Adam is the first man created

explanation.surface: A forward young girl marries the first man who comes along.
explanation.definitionFit: A bossy or forward young girl is called a little madam.

clue.text: From stage I shall remove this female entertainer

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow
remove this tells the solver to extract the answer from inside stage I shall

explanation.surface: A performer announces she will take herself off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation is an entertainer.

clue.text: Offspring — son produced by pop

parts.note: to pop something is British slang for pawning it

explanation.surface: A son is born to a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like father but is old British slang for pledging goods at a pawnbroker's.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn can mean the young or offspring of a person, often disparagingly.

clue.text: Influential teacher you are said to find in good university

indicators.note: in places the spoken phrase inside the other letters
said asks for the phrase to be heard, as in text-speak letters

parts.note: you are is heard as the letters U R

explanation.surface: A mentor of yours can be found at a fine university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns 'you are' into U R, which 'in' places between G and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a revered spiritual or intellectual guide.

clue.text: For example, turning back cover can make one cold

indicators.note: turning back reverses the abbreviation for for example

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Turning back a blanket can make someone feel cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid is a literary word for icy.

clue.text: Measure by legal authority enclosed area

indicators.note: by puts the measure next to the legal authority

parts.note: a court is a body with legal authority
a yard is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A legal body measures out a fenced-off patch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is open ground enclosed by walls or buildings.

clue.text: Bob disappeared when this was launched on D-day

definitions.text: Bob disappeared when this was launched on D-day

parts.words: Bob disappeared when this was launched on D-day
parts.note: Bob is slang for the shilling, withdrawn when Britain's money switched to a hundred-pence pound on Decimal Day, 15 February 1971

explanation.walkthrough: D-day sounds like the 1944 invasion, but here it is Decimal Day in 1971; a bob was a shilling, an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A money system based on tens replaced pounds, shillings and pence in Britain.
